surfaced_pitfalls.finding: cargo-ci is not deterministic under host load. crates/server/tests/server_integration/graceful_shutdown_tests.rs::test_jit_server_shutdown_force_closes_a_stalled_connection_and_exits_zero failed the gate for 3e340587 with 'the stalled connection was dropped before the drain deadline' at load average 6-10 (a worker build running beside the gate). It passes 5/5 in isolation on the same commit. The assertion is that a stalled connection SURVIVES to a drain deadline, which is precisely what CPU contention breaks.
surfaced_pitfalls.disposition: Not attributed to any wave-0 diff. Operationally: do not run worker builds concurrently with the gate pipeline for the rest of this container, and re-evaluate the affected gate on a quiet host rather than accepting or bypassing the failure. Worth a standalone issue at epic close — a timing-sensitive test inside the authoritative whole-workspace gate makes every issue's verdict load-dependent. Related to the known env-sensitivity of the commands::gate* lib tests.
surfaced_pitfalls.correction: Superseded: the failure is NOT load-induced flakiness. The test spends up to three consecutive 2s wait_for_close budgets after SIGTERM before asserting the stalled connection is still open, while GRACEFUL_DRAIN_TIMEOUT is 5s — so once those waits exceed 5s a CORRECT server has already force-closed the survivor and the assertion fails on conforming behaviour. It failed 2/2 whole-workspace runs including one on an idle host, and passes 10/10 in isolation. Fixed lead-direct at owner direction. The earlier 'do not run worker builds beside the gate' advice still stands on its own merits but was not the cause here.

The edits do not overlap textually, so git merged all three cleanly. scripts/verify-commit-builds.sh reported the merge commit as building and was right to: its contract is `cargo build --workspace`, which never compiles #[cfg(test)] code, and the broken call site is inside a `mod tests`. cargo-ci caught it one gate cycle later. Separately, 6c47b99a's tagged ProfileOrigin encoding broke mcp-server/test-integration.js:456, which asserted the bare string; the mcp-ci gate the lead added to that issue caught it.
surfaced_pitfalls.disposition: Both fixed lead-direct on main with per-issue attribution (a89586ec, b558fa4f) so each lands in its own issue's review footprint. The verify-commit-builds gap is real and unfiled: a merge that breaks only test targets passes the guard. `cargo test --workspace --no-run` would close it. The session-3 handoff's stronger claim — that the guard is vacuous because a cold build cannot finish in 24-30s — is NOT what this incident shows and remains unverified.

surfaced_pitfalls.text: jit-dogfood's packaged [namespaces.satisfies] contribution still carries the pre-amendment one-line description, while .jit/config.toml carries the sharpened one the owner ruled in session 5. A package re-apply would overwrite the ruling. [namespaces.per] is in neither package and is repository-local only. Whoever reduces the packages (e4ba28c5) or applies one to this repository must reconcile both.
surfaced_pitfalls.disposition: CLOSED session 8 at commit a1fb4e4f. Reconciled while gating 93fef456: its REQ-03 names the vocabulary the workflow package adds, and a packaged namespace declaration that would overwrite the owner's ruling on re-apply is inside that subject, so it was closed before the container gate rather than carried as a follow-up. [namespaces.per] stays repository-local by the session-5 ruling and is correctly in neither package.

surfaced_pitfalls.text: `cargo test --workspace --no-run` does not catch a cross-branch break that compiles and fails at run time. Session 5's handoff proposed it as the fix for the verify-commit-builds gap; it closed the compile half only. c7058cac and 6c47b99a merged into a tree that compiled and whose profile acceptance test panicked. Run the suite, not the build.

Editing a live consumer mid-pipeline trips the stale-binary guard on every subsequent gate with exit 10. contrib/gates/ is not a build input, but its packaged mirror under profiles/jit-dogfood/assets/live/ is, and the drift assertion requires editing both. Two of c7058cac's gates were refused this way. Make live-consumer edits between pipelines, never during one.

merge-and-gate.sh cleared incremental state at -maxdepth 2, which misses the nested target dirs tests create (target/init-commands/debug/incremental, target/jit-stale-child-test-cache/debug/incremental). cargo-ci's post-run incremental-state check finds them and fails the gate. The session copy now sweeps at -maxdepth 4.

A worker citing an invariant as its reason to defer is worth checking against what the invariant says. 0cf1f351 cited @/invariant/convention-convergence for NOT changing a shared method's matching base, when that invariant prescribes changing the shared form at its source. Reading it correctly turned a deferral into a two-commit fix.

A worker's targeted-target pass is not evidence for the target. 60c211d6 changed a pub(crate) helper in doc_show_tests.rs that artifact_conformance_cli_tests.rs imports, ran only its own module, and reported the sibling's failure as an 'unrelated baseline failure'. It failed cargo-ci on main. Briefs now require the whole target plus a base-commit control before any baseline claim.

The lead chose a reading of a criteria conflict instead of escalating, exactly as session 3's trap forbids, and briefed ten workers with it. The gate ruled the other way and two issues lost a round. A criteria conflict noticed at DISPATCH time is the same escalation as one noticed at review time — the trap is not limited to lead review.

Sharpening [namespaces.per] and the review prompt fixed 39c34568's label over-reach but NOT 6c47b99a's: that reviewer stopped citing the label and cited the decision text directly. The amendment addressed a narrower thing than the pattern. Resequencing — landing the issue that actually delivers the decision — is what has worked both times.

The lead's own brief created a soundness hole in 32779829: it instructed that ignored files must never enter a gate's input digest, so git ls-files --exclude-standard silently drops web/node_modules, which npm-ci genuinely reads. A dependency change would move that checker's verdict without moving the digest. Exclusion must be declared, not inherited from the ignore rules. Review a brief's own instructions when a finding lands on them.

Amending a container decision does not sweep the leaf criteria written against the old decision. Session 6 amended D-20 (invariant moves into jit-default) and expanded c7058cac to deliver it, but e4ba28c5's REQ-04 still named the kind the amendment removed. Caught at dispatch by measuring the two manifests, not by reading the criterion. After any decision amendment, re-read every not-yet-dispatched leaf that cites that decision.

The session-1 trap repeated in a new place: 5d12a79f swept every adopter markdown page its change invalidated (cli-commands.md, profiles.md, events.md, curated-tools.json) and still left the defect, because the stale text was a Rust string literal in crates/jit/src/output.rs that RENDERS INTO a generated reference page. A markdown-only sweep cannot find it and the generated page must not be hand-edited. When a change moves an error's meaning, grep the description tables in output.rs, not docs/.

code-review reads an issue's RECORDED GATE EVIDENCE, not only its diff, so gate order inside the pipeline changes the verdict. Running it first cost two review rounds: 0db28190's REQ-04 ('the mechanical documentation checks pass') was failed while docs-mechanical sat queued behind the reviewer and passed twelve seconds later, and fd61b44f's REQ-03 was failed for having one cargo-ci execution on record. merge-and-gate.sh now sorts code-review last. Corollary: evidence the lead gathers in its own terminal does not exist as far as the reviewer is concerned — 32779829's verdict reuse means a second `jit gate evaluate` will NOT produce a second execution record unless --force is passed.

A worker can hand-roll around a shared primitive it never found. 7d038e97 wrote check-then-rename publication when crates/jit/src/storage/external_publish.rs already exposed publish_external_directory_noreplace over renameat2/RENAME_NOREPLACE. The brief named the invariant but not the primitive; naming the invariant is not enough, because the worker satisfied its own reading of it. Name the function.

A worker citing CODE PATHS is not evidence for a criterion about an OUTCOME. d35cc3f2 cited init.rs:93-97 as satisfying 'initialization succeeds'; building the binary and running the command showed it failing and applying half the configuration. When a criterion names an outcome, require the command and its observed result.

A test edited to supply what the default path lacks is masking a regression, and the tell is in the diff. e4ba28c5 changed four `location: None` call sites to a supplied location; its tests passed while `jit init --profile jit-dogfood` stayed broken for adopters. The lead read those edits as scope creep, verified they were inside mod tests, and moved on. `-location: None` / `+location: Some(...)` is a question, not a detail.

setsid nohup codex workers notify nothing — no idle ping, no exit notification. Two ran unwatched this session and one failed instantly against a nonexistent worktree without anyone noticing. Attach a completion watcher at dispatch time.

dispatch-worker-worktree.sh correctly refused a dirty tree and the lead's filtering grep discarded the error, so the codex dispatch that followed died against a nonexistent directory. Never pipe that script through a filter.

A latent defect can pass every gate because nothing reaches it. initialize_fresh_repository captured the layout before publishing and applied the rest of the closure against the stale capture; unreachable until a package declared a dependency, so 7835fdc0's gates were all green over it. Fixed in d35cc3f2 by rebinding the tracked layout after publication, only when the roots match, so the reentry guard still rejects a genuinely different selection.

session_notes.note: Codex CLI workers cannot commit: codex-cli 0.146.0 makes .git read-only under -s workspace-write, and neither -c sandbox_workspace_write.writable_roots nor --add-dir lifts it (verified on a throwaway repo in /tmp as well as in a worktree). Worker briefs therefore forbid git writes and the lead commits each worker's worktree diff onto its branch with the jit:<short-id> attribution the code-review gate reads. --add-dir DOES work for non-.git paths, so $HOME/.cargo, $HOME/.cache and $HOME/.npm are granted or cargo cannot take its package-cache lock. jit read-only commands (item show, issue show, validate) work unmodified inside the sandbox.

Session 4 ended without a handoff. Reconstructed from git log, .jit state and the gate-run records: it merged and gated the wave-0 tail (a30d704d, then reworks for 09aea8b3 and 510297e4), fixed the graceful-shutdown drain test twice, marked it #[ignore]d against the new issue fd61b44f, and amended [namespaces.satisfies]. Its merge with 6c47b99a is a cross-branch regression — c7058cac's test_apply_embedded_profile_jit_default_reproduces_the_scaffolded_configuration applies profiles/jit-default read from the real checkout, and 6c47b99a's apply now refuses a package directory outside the TARGET repository's worktree. `cargo test --workspace --no-run` passed on the merged tree and did not catch it: the pair compiles, it fails at run time. Lead fixes the one call site on main. The ten adoptions were re-dispatched on fresh -r1 worktrees off a3291826; their old branches hold one superseded commit each (SHAs in the session scratchpad's discarded-wip-sha.txt) because branch deletion is blocked in this harness.

Adoption footprints were not what the issue Notes implied in two cases. 76b16af0's four call sites are commands/config.rs, validation/repository.rs and two in storage/json.rs (confirmed by a read-only codex spark pass against the Notes' 'four call sites across three modules'); its first worker instead took profile.rs and validate.rs, and its profile.rs edit destroyed the subject of c7058cac's scaffold-comparison test. be918f22 legitimately owns config.rs as a repository-inspection module, so 76b16af0-r2's config.rs hunk is the redundant one at merge. Measure a footprint before dispatch; the Notes' counts are advisory.

owner_preferences.preference: Gate one issue at a time and report per issue.
owner_preferences.note: Costs nothing: verdict reuse means the expensive part is merging several issues before any gating, not gating them separately. Batching merges is still fine when stated explicitly, with per-issue verdicts reported.

owner_preferences.preference: Choose the worker model case by case, not by rule.
owner_preferences.note: Explicitly corrected the lead's over-generalisation of 'use Opus for reworks' into a blanket policy. Codex gpt-5.6-luna for first attempts on clearly-specified work and for reworks whose sites and correct end state are both named; Opus when the work needs diagnosis, generalising past the named instance, or establishing an outcome. State which and why at each dispatch.
